oracle: astropy 6.1.7 (coordinates.get_body_barycentric, time) with numpy 2.2.6 and scipy 1.15.3
identity: Independent, cited implementations; no Gravitas code ran: astropy.coordinates.get_body_barycentric('earth') with the built-in ephemeris (ERFA epv00 of pyerfa 2.0.1.5, nothing downloaded), astropy.time (ERFA time-scale conversions, leap-second table), scipy.optimize.least_squares (method lm, the exact spherical five-parameter astrometric model of a source with constant barycentric velocity, the normalised vector from the Earth to the source), scipy.optimize.curve_fit with absolute sigmas (straight lines in the tangent plane), numpy.random.default_rng (the noise).
index: https://pypi.org/simple (pip default index; no mirror, no pip.conf, no PIP_* variable); the virtual environment is Prompt 180's, in which nothing was added for this prompt
install: python3.10 -m venv <scratchpad>/oracle180; <venv>/bin/python -m pip install --only-binary :all: numpy scipy astropy photutils (the resolved versions above); the venv is not committed and no package is
run: cd <empty scratchpad directory>; <venv>/bin/python -I tools/astrometric-series-oracle/oracle.py tools/astrometric-series-oracle/oracle-inputs.json tests/fixtures/astrometric-series/oracle-results.json; then Prettier
committedBefore: thresholds.json and ASTROMETRY.md's contract were committed before the oracle's inputs and script existed, and the oracle's inputs, script and results were committed before js/measure/astrometric-series.js existed

parameters.model: x(t) = D (p0 + m (t - t0)) with D = 648000 / (pi parallax) au, p0 the unit vector of (ra, dec), m = mu_a* e_alpha + mu_d e_delta in radians per Julian year, t0 the first epoch; the apparent direction is (x - r_Earth) normalised, r_Earth the barycentric position in au from astropy; no aberration, no light deflection, no light time
parameters.noise: numpy.random.default_rng(noiseSeed): sigma-scaled normals, first the n right ascension offsets (divided by cos dec) and then the n declination offsets, in arcseconds
parameters.sphericalFit: scipy.optimize.least_squares(method='lm', x_scale='jac', xtol=ftol=gtol=1e-15), parameters the offsets in arcseconds of the first-epoch position from the truth, mu_a*, mu_d and the parallax, started at 1.05, 0.95 and 1.1 times the truth; residuals in sigma units; covariance inv(J^T J)
parameters.lineFit: xi and eta (arcsec) of a gnomonic projection about the normalised mean of the unit vectors; the weighted mean epoch as reference; scipy.optimize.curve_fit(absolute_sigma=True, an analytic Jacobian, started at 0.1 and 0.1)
parameters.times: astropy.time.Time(jd, format='jd', scale='utc'), .tt and .tdb; offsets in seconds from the two-part Julian dates

conventions: angles in degrees, epochs TDB Julian dates, positions in au in the ICRS-aligned equatorial frame, proper motion mu_a* in arcseconds per Julian year (the right-ascension rate times cos dec)
references: Harris, C. R. et al. 2020, Nature 585, 357 (numpy)
Virtanen, P. et al. 2020, Nature Methods 17, 261 (scipy)
Wallace, P. T. and Capitaine, N. 2006, A&A 459, 981; SOFA/ERFA epv00 (the Earth's barycentric ephemeris)
Lindegren, L. et al. 2012, A&A 538, A78 (the standard astrometric model of a single star)
